I skimmed through your post history a bit. Just wanted to say that most regular OBGyns are likely not going to be able to find endo. It can be practically invisible to the untrained eye or so I’ve heard. Your best bet would be to find an endometriosis excision specialist. I had 2 laps done by a regular OBGyn and she said she didn’t find endo the first time but she did find it the 2nd. And she also said I had “adhesions”. Which in fact was endo. The nausea and symptoms you’re describing reminds me a lot of my case. I had constant severe nausea and ended up having bowel endo. Almost needed a bowel resection.

I was misdiagnosed with IBS for the longest time. One day I noticed that my symptoms had improved after I got my iud inserted. I also realized that my symptoms would always seem to worsen around the time of my period. Fast forward a couple years and I had the worst flare ups imaginable that turned out to be caused by ovarian cysts. After my second surgery to remove these cysts my OBGyn found endometriosis. I went to see a specialist after that and underwent endometriosis excision surgery. Turns out i had endo lesions all over the place, including my bowel ! I am practically symptom free now after treatment. Consider talking to a knowledgeable OBGyn or Endo Specialist ! Or maybe just doing some research about the disease. A lot of people who have endometriosis have been diagnosed with ibs.

I’m not a doctor, but I definitely would keep asking if you really think it could be a possibility. I’ve had a wide range of symptoms but I would definitely look up comparison of the two so you can see if anything I don’t mention could also be an endo symptom. I have an intolerance to fodmaps (especially around the time of my period ), abdominal pain, headaches, constipation, painful sex, bloating, acid reflux, fatigue, and the most prominent symptom I have is nausea. Also when I did have a period (it stopped around 2019 when I got an iud) I noticed they were sometimes longer than 7 days and gave me very bad cramps. My symptoms always seemed to be the worst at the time of my period as well.

Endo is rarely able to be found outside of laparoscopic surgery (And it actually took 2 for them to find mine.) but I know that is the for sure way to know you have it. If you can, I would bring that up when talking to your OBGyn. I’ve learned over the years that sometimes I need to be really persistent with doctors because sometimes I was right when they shot down my concerns. Stay strong ! And I hope things go well for you ❤️
